rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration with key components (scgpt RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) to establish performance and isolate the impact of critical design choices. This configuration balances exploration of advanced encoders and standard aggregation/fusion methods, providing a foundation for comparing other variations.

The existing evidence shows that config_005 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat) achieves 0.507 validation accuracy. This experiment tests changing fusion from 'concat' to 'weighted' while keeping other parameters identical. This isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and could reveal if weighted fusion improves performance. It balances exploration (testing a key component) and exploitation (building on the existing multimodal/multiprofile setup).

Existing evidence shows that weighted fusion (config_010) outperforms concat fusion (config_005). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from transformer to avgpool (while keeping RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion method consistent with config_010) improves performance. It isolates the impact of aggregation strategy, a critical design choice, and builds on the promising weighted fusion approach.

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_018) yield the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (while keeping avgpool and weighted fusion) improves performance. It isolates the effect of the image encoder, a key design choice, and builds on the promising aggregation/fusion combination. This balances exploitation of current strong evidence with exploration of a critical component.

The existing evidence shows that config_018 (avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping RNA encoder (scgpt) and image encoder (resnet50) consistent. This isolates the effect of aggregation method, a key design choice, to determine if transformer aggregation could improve performance further. It balances exploitation (building on config_018's successful components) and exploration (testing a critical hyperparameter).

Existing evidence shows that avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_018) yield high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder (scgpt → pca_n2000) while keeping other components (resnet50 image encoder, avgpool, weighted fusion) constant clarifies the impact of RNA representation choices. It isolates a key design decision (RNA encoder) with minimal changes, balancing exploration of critical factors against exploitation of promising configurations.

Existing evidence shows pca_n2000 (RNA) and resnet50 (image) combinations (config_017) achieve high accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while retaining pca_n2000/resnet50 and weighted fusion. It isolates the effect of aggregation method on performance, building on the strong foundation of successful RNA/image encoder pairing. This balances exploitation of proven components with exploration of aggregation strategies.

The existing evidence shows that config_017 (pca_n2000 RNA, ResNet50 image, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.638999). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation method the same) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, which is critical for understanding model behavior without altering other design choices. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly addresses a key design decision with minimal parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image encoders, along with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, achieve high accuracy (config_017: 0.639). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with the same RNA/image encoders but concat fusion, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It addresses uncertainty about whether transformer aggregation could improve performance while maintaining the high-performing RNA/image encoder combination.

Existing evidence shows that config_017 (PCA_n2000 RNA, ResNet50 image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether using ImageNet ViT_L image encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion (vs ResNet50) could improve performance, isolating the impact of image encoder choice. It balances exploration by testing a key design decision (image encoder) while keeping RNA encoder and profile settings aligned with top performers.
